audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Yasuo/Yasuo/Skill/Skill/Yasuo/Yasuo — Yasuo winning four of seven stages. Packet says Gnar,Gnar,Gnar,Gnar,Skill,Gnar,Yasuo, the win rate is 52.75% in Gnar's favour over 1020 games, and every whys[] entry describes Gnar winning the stage it is attached to.
audit.why: whys[1] says the level-2 poke is one 'his crit autos can't trade back into' — the page marks that stage YASUO. whys[2] says 'his minion-dash can't catch a Mini that just holds range' — marked YASUO. whys[5] says 'Mini's ranged poke keeps the lead' — marked YASUO. This is the most severe chart inversion in the slice: the enum tells the reader they are losing a lane the prose, the packet and the win rate all say they are winning.
audit.corrected: Gnar / Gnar / Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Gnar / Yasuo, proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer spikes said 'Stridebreaker'; Yasuo's actual spike structure is Wind Wall's cooldown decay and his two-item crit timing.
audit.why: Wind Wall starts at 25s and only reaches 17s at rank 5, so early it is a genuine 25-second window where Mini poke is free — that is why levels 1-5 belong to Gnar. His real takeover is two crit items, which the content layer already dates correctly.
audit.corrected: Phase whys now key to Wind Wall's cooldown and the two-item crit spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the full layer never names Yasuo's abilities in mechanical terms and never states Wind Wall's cooldown or 4-second duration. It also never mentions Way of the Wanderer's shield, the flagged missing interaction.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1, 17s at rank 5, and stands for only 4 seconds — those three numbers are the whole reason 'bait it and poke' works and the page states none of them. Steel Tempest is a flat 4s cooldown that only knocks up at 2 stacks, which is the actual tell for his all-in. And his passive shield builds while he MOVES, so it is always up when he walks at you — committing Mega into a full shield wastes the transform window.
audit.corrected: Stated Wind Wall 25s/4s and that Wallop's melee smash passes through it, Steel Tempest's 4s and 2-stack knockup, and the moving passive shield that must be chipped off before you commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page says whether Wind Wall blocks Gnar's GNAR! (R). Every current line says only 'Wind Wall can't block Mega knockup', which is ambiguous between Wallop (W) and GNAR! (R).
audit.why: Gnar's R carries a derived 'projectile' flag in the kit file, but Riot's own description is 'throws everything around him in a chosen direction' — a displacement, not a projectile. Per the standing rule, when a derived flag contradicts the description I trust the description. But that still leaves the actual Wind Wall interaction unknown, and it is the single highest-value unknown in this matchup: whether you can wall-fling a Yasuo who holds W decides every level-6 commit.
audit.corrected: No claim written either way. I kept all edits scoped to Wallop (W), which is unambiguously a melee smash and unblockable, and removed no existing text about R.

notes: Worst chart inversion found in this slice: the page told a Gnar player he loses levels 2, 3 and the first-item stage to Yasuo, while its own whys[] text, the packet chart and a 52.75% win rate over 1020 games all say Gnar wins them. Four content enums and four full-layer sides flipped as one group. Packet defect (never names Yasuo's abilities) is fixed with real numbers: Wind Wall 25s/17s and its 4-second duration, Steel Tempest's flat 4s and 2-stack knockup, and the passive shield that builds while moving. DELIBERATE OMISSION: I wrote nothing about whether Wind Wall blocks GNAR! (R). Gnar's R carries a derived 'projectile' flag, but Riot's description calls it throwing everything around him in a direction — a displacement. Per the rule that the description wins over a misfiring flag, I did not assert 'projectile', and I did not assert the opposite either. All my Wind Wall copy is scoped strictly to Wallop (W), which is unambiguously a melee smash.
